chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, who said:

Sulayman ibn Khalid asked him (peace be upon him) and I was with him, about a man who circumambulated the House six circuits. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And how does he circumambulate six circuits?' He said: 'He faced the Stone and said, "Allah is the Greatest," and he committed to one (circuit). So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He should circumambulate one circuit.' He said: 'Supposing he loses it until he goes back to his family?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should instruct someone to circumambulate on his behalf.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone makes a mistake in counting their Tawaf circuits?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who mistakenly counts six circuits instead of seven by completing the seventh, illustrating the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in ritual acts. The Imam further permits sending a proxy (*na'ib*) to complete the missing circuit if the pilgrim is unable to do so personally, highlighting the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence for resolving ritual errors (*khata*).
